title: QuickBooks Online Pricing: Plans, Costs, and Choices
excerpt: QuickBooks Online pricing runs from $38 to $340 a month at list prices. See all four plans, the introductory discount, and the add-ons that raise your bill.
author: David Chen, CPA
content:
Shopping for accounting software starts with one question: what does it actually cost each month? QuickBooks Online pricing runs from $38 to $340 a month at Intuit's list prices, and the plan you pick decides how many people can use it, whether you get inventory and project tracking, and how much of your bookkeeping still needs a workaround. This guide lays out all four paid plans, the introductory discount, the add-ons that quietly raise the bill, and how to choose without overpaying.

QuickBooks Online is the most widely used small-business accounting software in the United States, which is why its pricing gets searched so often. But the list price is only the starting point. Intuit discounts the first three months for new customers, charges separately for payroll, and raised the prices of three of the four plans in August 2026 — so a price quoted in an old review may not match the checkout page today. The figures in this guide are the list prices verified against Intuit's pricing page in November 2026; confirm them on Intuit's site before you buy, because Intuit changes prices without much warning.

QuickBooks Online Pricing at a Glance

There are four paid plans, and the ladder is simple: more money buys more users and more features. Simple Start costs $38 a month and allows one user. Essentials costs $85 a month and allows three users. Plus costs $140 a month and allows five users. Advanced costs $340 a month and allows up to 25 users. Those are the monthly list prices when you pay month to month, with no discount applied.

New customers usually do not pay those prices at first. Intuit offers 50 percent off for the first three months on paid plans, which brings the first-year totals to $399 for Simple Start, $892.50 for Essentials, $1,470 for Plus, and $3,570 for Advanced. That is three months at half price and nine months at full price. Do not annualize the discounted rate — the fourth month is the one that matters, because that is the price you will keep paying.

Two other facts belong in any honest price comparison. First, the August 2026 increase hit Essentials, Plus, and Advanced; Simple Start stayed at $38. If your renewal went up this fall, that is why. Second, Intuit also lists a free tier with tight limits — one user, a small number of invoices a month, and a single bank connection. It suits a side gig with a handful of transactions, not a business with payroll, inventory, or a team.

What Each QuickBooks Online Pricing Plan Includes

Simple Start is the entry point for full double-entry accounting. It covers invoicing and payments, automated bank feeds, income and expense tracking, bill management, basic reporting, receipt capture, mileage tracking, and sales tax. For a one-person business that sends invoices and tracks expenses, it is genuinely enough — the limits show up only when a second person needs to post transactions, because Simple Start allows exactly one user plus accountant access.

Essentials adds the things a small team needs: three users instead of one, enhanced bill management, multiple currencies, and the ability to add employee time to invoices. The jump from $38 to $85 a month is mostly a user-count and bill-management jump. If your business pays vendors regularly, works in more than one currency, or bills clients for staff time, Essentials is where the plans start to feel like a real accounting system rather than a solo ledger.

Plus adds inventory tracking, project profitability, budgeting, and class and location tracking, with five users. This is the plan for businesses that sell physical products or run jobs they need to price properly. Inventory alone justifies the step up for a retailer: without it, you are tracking stock in a spreadsheet and reconciling it by hand at month end. A full year of Plus at list price is $1,680, or $1,470 with the introductory discount.

Advanced adds batch invoicing and expenses, workflow automation, custom access controls, data restoration, custom key performance indicators, and 24/7 support, with 25 users. It also includes Bill Pay Elite at no extra subscription cost — approvals, an audit trail, and 1099 e-filing — which is a paid add-on on the three lower plans. Advanced is for a business with a finance team, not a solo owner, and the $340 a month reflects that.

The Introductory Discount: What New Customers Actually Pay

The first thing to understand about the price you will actually pay is the introductory offer. New customers get 50 percent off for three months, and the discount applies to the subscription only. It does not cover payroll per-employee fees, state tax filing fees, or other add-ons, so payroll stays at full price from day one. At the end of the three months, the subscription moves to the list price in force at that time — which may not be the list price you saw at signup if Intuit raises prices in between.

Intuit typically lets a new customer choose between a 30-day free trial and the 50 percent discount for three months. You pick one at signup, not both. The trial is the better choice if you want to test the software with your own data before committing; the discount is the better choice if you already know QuickBooks is the tool and want the lower bill. Either way, set a calendar reminder for the month the discount ends, because the jump from $70 to $140 on Plus catches people by surprise.

Renewals are where the August 2026 increase still stings. If you subscribed before that date, your renewal price moved to the new list prices on or after August 1, 2026. There is no grandfathering on the paid plans, and the increase applies even if nothing about your usage changed. Check your subscription page rather than your memory: the price you paid last year is not necessarily the price you pay this year.

Add-Ons That Change Your Real Monthly Cost

The subscription is only part of the bill for most businesses. Payroll is the biggest add-on, and it is priced separately on every plan, with a per-employee fee on top of the base payroll subscription. A business with ten employees can easily pay more for payroll than for the accounting software itself, so price the two together before you commit.

Bill Pay Elite is $45 a month on Simple Start, Essentials, and Plus, and included on Advanced. If you pay many vendors by ACH, the approval workflow and audit trail may be worth it; if you pay three vendors a month by check, it is not. Payment processing is another separate cost: when customers pay invoices by card or bank transfer, Intuit takes a percentage of each payment, and those fees sit outside the subscription entirely.

Then there are the smaller costs that add up: extra users beyond your plan's limit, which force a plan upgrade rather than a per-seat purchase — a sixth billable user on Plus means moving to Advanced at $200 more a month, not buying one more seat. That is the single most expensive upgrade in the whole pricing ladder, and it is worth knowing before your team grows to six people.

How to Pick the Right Plan (and When to Switch)

Pick by the constraint that will bite first, not by the feature list. If you are a solo freelancer who invoices clients and tracks expenses, Simple Start is the right plan and the cheapest one — paying for Plus would buy inventory tracking you will never open. If a second person needs to post transactions, you need Essentials at minimum, because Simple Start allows only one user. If you sell products or track jobs, you need Plus for inventory and project profitability. If you have a finance team, custom roles, and batch workflows, Advanced is the only plan that offers them.

The other way to choose is by the number that matters most to your business: users, inventory items, or open invoices. Count the people who need to log in, not the people who will glance at a report — reports can go to anyone, but posting needs a seat. If the count is four or five, Plus fits today, but plan for the sixth user: that upgrade to Advanced costs $200 more a month, so a growing team should budget for it early.

Switching plans is straightforward and can be done from the subscription settings — upgrade when you need the features, downgrade when you do not. The honest test is your own books: if you are paying for Plus and have never opened the inventory screen, drop to Essentials and save $55 a month. If your books are clean and your statements reconcile, the plan is working. Frequently asked questions

What is the cheapest QuickBooks Online pricing plan?

Simple Start at $38 a month is the cheapest paid plan, with one user. New customers pay $19 a month for the first three months with the introductory discount. Intuit also lists a free tier with tight limits, but it is not a substitute for a paid plan once the business has real volume.

Does QuickBooks Online pricing include payroll?

No. Payroll is a separate add-on on every plan, with its own base price plus a per-employee fee. The introductory discount does not apply to payroll. Price the accounting subscription and payroll together before you commit, because payroll is often the larger of the two bills.

Can I switch QuickBooks Online plans later?

Yes. You can upgrade or downgrade from the subscription settings, and the change takes effect on the next billing cycle. Upgrade when you need more users or features, and downgrade when you are paying for features you never use — the software does not penalize you for moving down.

Why did my QuickBooks bill go up in 2026?

Intuit raised the list prices of Essentials, Plus, and Advanced for renewals on or after August 1, 2026. Simple Start did not change. If your renewal crossed that date, your bill moved to the new prices — $85, $140, and $340 a month respectively — even if your usage stayed the same.

Is there a free trial for QuickBooks Online?

Intuit typically offers either a 30-day free trial or 50 percent off the first three months — you choose one at signup. The trial is best for testing the software with your own data; the discount is best if you already know you want QuickBooks and would rather pay less for three months.

Start with the plan that fits the business you have today, not the one you hope to have next year: Simple Start for a solo operator, Essentials for a small team, Plus for products and projects, Advanced for a finance team.
